toolRoot.question: Where should the Godot editor, its export templates and editor data, the Android SDK and the downloads live? Give an absolute folder path on a drive with room for them (export templates alone are over 1 GB per build).

toolRoot.normalize: Replace every backslash in the user's answer with a forward slash and strip a trailing slash before deriving paths.

godot._note: Asset names below are the 4.7.2-stable release assets as listed by the GitHub API. Download each from releaseBase and compare its SHA-512 with the line for it in checksums.

builds._editorExecutable: After unpacking, {editorExe} is the editor binary in paths.editor: the single Godot_v*-stable* executable that is not the _console variant (Windows), the binary inside the .app bundle's Contents/MacOS (macOS), or the single Godot_v* file (Linux). A .NET archive unpacks into its own folder with the binary and its GodotSharp folder beside it; keep them together.
builds._editorConsoleExecutable: {editorConsoleExe} is the binary a scripted check runs. On Windows it is the _console variant beside {editorExe} (Godot_v*-stable*_console.exe): {editorExe} is a GUI-subsystem executable that returns at once with no captured output and no exit code, so a check run through it can never pass (QA #396). On macOS and Linux it is {editorExe} itself. The user still launches {editorExe}.
builds._templateArchive: A TPZ file is a zip archive. Its templates/ folder holds the template files and version.txt; their contents go into {paths.templates}/{templateFolder}.

selfContained._note: Per data_paths.html, a file named ._sc_ (or _sc_) next to the editor binary makes the editor keep its data, settings and cache in editor_data/ beside the binary. On macOS the binary is inside the .app bundle.

dotnet._note: minimumMajor is the floor the check accepts: the 4.7 C# docs need .NET SDK 8 or later, and 9 or later for Android export; 9 covers both. It is not the install target. .NET 8 and 9 reached end of support on 2026-11-10, so the Windows apply installs SDK 11 (STS, supported to 2028-11-14); a newer SDK builds a Godot 4.7 project, which keeps its own target framework.

sdkPackages._note: The packages are the sdkmanager line in exporting_for_android.html (stable, 4.7). Substitute {packages} with sdkPackages.packages.<os>, each package double-quoted. The id form follows the pinned cmdline-tools archive for that OS (QA #396): the Windows and Linux archives (16111833, cmdline-tools 23.0) ship sdkmanager as a wrapper over the Android CLI, whose ids use '/'; on Windows that wrapper is a cmd batch file, and cmd splits an unquoted 'build-tools;35.0.1' on ';' (PowerShell drops the quotes), installing only platform-tools and still exiting 0. The Linux wrapper maps ';' to '/' itself, so '/' is used there for the same build. The macOS archive (15641748, cmdline-tools 21.0) is the classic sdkmanager, which takes the documented ';' form. --list_installed prints ids in the same form, so each OS's check compares against its own list. Windows omits cmdline-tools/latest (QA #396): sdkmanager.bat runs android.exe from cmdline-tools/latest/bin, and asked to install cmdline-tools/latest it fails to extract over its own running android.exe, exits 1 and installs none of the packages. The android-cmdline-tools item's unpack already provides cmdline-tools/latest, and that item's check still requires it.

cmdlineTools._note: Same archives as react-native-android-setup's downloads.cmdlineTools (highest builds listed on 2026-10-17).

items.summary: The downloads, editor and Android SDK folders under the tool root.
The Godot editor for the project's language: builds.<godotLanguage>.editorArchive for this OS, checksum-verified and unpacked into paths.editor.

apply: (Get-FileHash '{paths.downloads}/{editorArchive}' -Algorithm SHA512).Hash  # must equal the line for {editorArchive} in {godot.checksums}
shasum -a 512 '{paths.downloads}/{editorArchive}'  # must equal the line for {editorArchive} in {godot.checksums}
sha512sum '{paths.downloads}/{editorArchive}'  # must equal the line for {editorArchive} in {godot.checksums}

items.summary: The selfContained.markerFile next to the editor binary, so the editor's data, settings and export templates live under paths.editorData instead of the user profile.
Export templates for the editor's exact version and build: builds.<godotLanguage>.exportTemplates, checksum-verified, its templates/ contents placed in {paths.templates}/{templateFolder}.

apply: (Get-FileHash '{paths.downloads}/{exportTemplates}' -Algorithm SHA512).Hash  # must equal the line for {exportTemplates} in {godot.checksums}
shasum -a 512 '{paths.downloads}/{exportTemplates}'  # must equal the line for {exportTemplates} in {godot.checksums}
sha512sum '{paths.downloads}/{exportTemplates}'  # must equal the line for {exportTemplates} in {godot.checksums}

items.summary: The .NET SDK the .NET editor builds C# with, at dotnet.minimumMajor or later.

windows.check: dotnet --list-sdks  # expect a version at dotnet.minimumMajor or later

macos.check: dotnet --list-sdks  # expect a version at dotnet.minimumMajor or later

linux.check: dotnet --list-sdks  # expect a version at dotnet.minimumMajor or later

items.summary: JDK 17, which the Android export docs recommend for compatibility and stability.
JAVA_HOME as a user variable pointing at the JDK 17 home, with forward slashes. The editor reads it as the default for its Java SDK Path.
Android command-line tools (sdkmanager) unpacked into downloads.cmdlineTools.installLayout.

windows.check: & '{paths.sdk}/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager.bat' --sdk_root='{paths.sdk}' --list_installed; $LASTEXITCODE  # expect exit 0 and a cmdline-tools/latest line; --version exits 1 on cmdline-tools 23.0 even when the tools work (QA #396)

items.summary: The SDK, platform, build-tools, NDK and CMake packages in sdkPackages.packages for this OS, installed into paths.sdk.
ANDROID_HOME as a user variable pointing at paths.sdk, plus platform-tools on PATH. The editor reads ANDROID_HOME as the default for its Android SDK Path.

The editor's export/android/java_sdk_path and export/android/android_sdk_path (Editor Settings > Export > Android: Java SDK Path, Android SDK Path). In Godot 4.7 they default to JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME when the editor settings file does not already hold them, so with self-contained mode a first launch from a new terminal picks both up. If the settings file in paths.editorData already holds other values, the user sets them in Editor Settings.

windows.check: Select-String -Path '{paths.editorData}/editor_settings-*.tres' -Pattern 'export/android/(java|android)_sdk_path' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue  # absent: defaults come from JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME; present: values must equal them
windows.apply: Open a new terminal so JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME are set, then launch '{editorExe}' once and close it

macos.check: grep -E 'export/android/(java|android)_sdk_path' '{paths.editorData}'/editor_settings-*.tres  # absent: defaults come from JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME; present: values must equal them
macos.apply: Open a new terminal so JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME are set, then launch '{editorExe}' once and close it

linux.check: grep -E 'export/android/(java|android)_sdk_path' '{paths.editorData}'/editor_settings-*.tres  # absent: defaults come from JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME; present: values must equal them
linux.apply: Open a new terminal so JAVA_HOME and ANDROID_HOME are set, then launch '{editorExe}' once and close it

verify._description: Run after every apply phase, and on its own when the user asks whether the host is ready. Each check reports pass or fail; the install is verified only when every check passes.

checks.summary: The installed editor runs headless and reports the configured version.
checks.pass: Exit code 0, and the first output line starts with {godot.version}.{godot.status} (followed by .mono for the C# build).

checks.summary: Export templates exist for that exact editor version and build.
For an Android target: JDK 17 and the SDK packages are present where the editor will look.
checks.pass: JAVA_HOME's java reports version 17, and sdkmanager --list_installed under ANDROID_HOME lists every package in sdkPackages.packages for this OS.
